developing and demonstrating a novel optical sensor system for sUAS state estimation that has high precision, high update rates, low power consumption, and is eye‐safe.
the development of a low power, non‐laser, eye safe optical beacon sensor for small unmanned aerial vehicle (sUAV) state estimation.
the design, development, and testing of an optical beacon system for use as a sensor for small unmanned aerial system (sUAV) state estimation.

the prototype sensor is an effective, low‐power, small‐footprint, low‐cost sensor system that provides a reference vector direction in a small UAS body frame, and that this sensor is suitable for use in sUAS attitude determination and state estimation systems, or as a component in other systems such as precision sUAS landings.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a small, low‐cost, eye‐safe beacon sensor has been developed that provides accurate, high update rate measurements of a reference vector direction in daylight conditions.
the prototype sensor can be used to validate sUAS attitude information, and the sensor system may also provide an inexpensive, lightweight, low‐power, and low‐cost method for sUAS state estimation.

the prototype system can measure the direction of a reference vector with high accuracy and without drift over a wide range of operating conditions, and it can do this using a low‐cost, low‐power, eye‐safe, nonlaser optical sensor system.
